native_result.query: What proportion of original studies in Experimental Economics were conducted in the United Kingdom?
native_result.HypoA: The original studies in Experimental Economics were primarily conducted in the United States (61.1%), while the replication studies were more distributed across countries like Austria (27.8%), Germany (11.1%), Singapore (27.8%), the United Kingdom (11.1%), and the United States (22.2%).
native_result.HypoB: Approximately 5.6% (1 out of 18) of original studies in the Experimental Economics replication project (project == "ee") were conducted in the United Kingdom, as recorded in the experiment_country.o column: the single UK study is ee.13 (Huck, Seltzer & Wallace, 2011, 'Deferred compensation in multiperiod labor contracts', American Economic Review). The vast majority of ee originals (11/18, 61%) were conducted in the United States, with the rest in Germany, Switzerland, Australia, and Austria; no country values are missing and no spelling variants of 'United Kingdom' occur in the ee subset.
native_result.WorkflowB: 1) Loaded meta-regression_study_data_heterogeneity_in_replication_projects.csv (927 rows; project distribution: ml1 592, ml3 220, rpp 97, ee 18). 2) Filtered project == 'ee' and excluded drop == True (none in ee): 18 rows. 3) Verified unit of analysis: 18 unique id, 18 unique title — no duplicates, 1 row = 1 original study. 4) Normalized experiment_country.o (variant mapping UK/England/Great Britain → 'United Kingdom' as safety net; only 'United Kingdom' occurs in ee; 0 missing values). 5) Numerator = unique ids with country == 'United Kingdom' → 1 (ee.13); denominator = 18 unique ids with known country → proportion = 1/18 = 0.0556 (5.6%). 6) Sensitivity checks: treating missing as not-UK (identical, 0 missing), counting by rows instead of ids (identical), cross-check with us_lab.o (US rows = us_lab.o 1, UK row us_lab.o = 0 — consistent). 7) Confirmed the replication_success dataset contains no country columns. Analysis executed in analysis_ee_uk.py; outputs in ee_uk_analysis.json.

sub_hypo.context: Original and replication studies in Experimental Economics.
sub_hypo.relations: The geographic distribution differs between original and replication studies: 61.1% of original studies were conducted in the United States, whereas replication studies were distributed across Austria (27.8%), Germany (11.1%), Singapore (27.8%), the United Kingdom (11.1%), and the United States (22.2%).

gold_sub_hypo.full_hypo: The original studies in Experimental Economics were primarily conducted in the United States (61.1%), while the replication studies were more distributed across countries like Austria (27.8%), Germany (11.1%), Singapore (27.8%), the United Kingdom (11.1%), and the United States (22.2%).

sub_hypo.text: Approximately 5.6% (1 of 18) of original studies in the Experimental Economics replication project were conducted in the United Kingdom. The single UK study was ee.13: Huck, Seltzer & Wallace (2011), 'Deferred compensation in multiperiod labor contracts', American Economic Review.
sub_hypo.context: Original studies with project == 'ee', excluding drop == True (none excluded); 18 unique studies with known country, one row per original study and no duplicate ids or titles.
sub_hypo.relations: The number of unique study ids with experiment_country.o == 'United Kingdom' divided by the number with known country is 1/18 = 0.0556 (5.6%); the sole matching id is ee.13.

sub_hypo.text: Most Experimental Economics original studies were conducted in the United States (11/18, approximately 61%); apart from the single United Kingdom study, the remaining studies were conducted in Germany, Switzerland, Australia, and Austria.
sub_hypo.context: The 18 unique original studies with project == 'ee', excluding drop == True (none excluded).
sub_hypo.relations: The United States accounts for 11 of 18 original studies (approximately 61%), the United Kingdom for one, and Germany, Switzerland, Australia, and Austria collectively for the remaining six.

sub_hypo.text: No original-study country values are missing and no spelling variants of 'United Kingdom' occur in the Experimental Economics subset.
sub_hypo.context: The 18 original studies with project == 'ee', excluding drop == True (none excluded); normalization mapped UK, England, and Great Britain to United Kingdom as a safety net.
sub_hypo.relations: There are zero missing country values; the only observed UK designation is 'United Kingdom', so variant normalization does not change the UK count.

The vast majority of ee originals (11/18, 61%) were conducted in the United States, with the rest in Germany, Switzerland, Australia, and Austria; no country values are missing and no spelling variants of 'United Kingdom' occur in the ee subset.
